texts.li: A file of {FACTION}'s pilgrims has stopped at the gate on its way to {PLACE}, {X_nameDef} at its head with a staff hung with shells. They ask whether anyone of the colony would walk with them: {TALE} there and back, on foot, and home with a shell of the shrine. {X_nameDef} looks longest at {A_nameDef}.

[grief] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has brought a file of pilgrims to the gate, bound for {PLACE}. {X_pronoun} has heard what {A_nameDef} carries, and says the road is good for a grief: {TALE} there and back with the fellowship, and a shell to bring home.

[guilt] Pilgrims of {FACTION} are resting at the gate on the road to {PLACE}. {X_nameDef}, who leads them, says that a walk to a shrine has eased heavier things than whatever {A_nameDef} is carrying, and that there is room in the file for one more: {TALE} there and back.

[doubt] {X_nameDef}, a keeper of {FACTION}'s pilgrims, has stopped at the gate with a file bound for {PLACE}. Faith is steadier for walking, {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef}, and anyone of the colony is welcome to walk with them: {TALE} there and back.

[relic,second] A file of {FACTION}'s pilgrims has come to the gate, bound for {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} says the relic is shown to walkers only, and anyone of the colony who walks with them, {A_nameDef} or {B_nameDef}, will see it: {TALE} there and back.

[relic,!second] A file of {FACTION}'s pilgrims has come to the gate, bound for {PLACE}. The relic is shown to walkers only, {X_nameDef} says, and {A_nameDef} could see it if {A_pronoun} walked with them: {TALE} there and back.

[old,second] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has stopped at the gate with pilgrims bound for {PLACE}, a shrine older than any of the peoples. They would take one of the colony with them, {X_pronoun} says, {TALE} there and back on foot, if {A_nameDef} or {B_nameDef} would come.

[old,!second] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has stopped at the gate with pilgrims bound for {PLACE}, a shrine older than any of the peoples, and asks whether {A_nameDef} would walk with them: {TALE} there and back on foot.

[lowtech] Pilgrims of {FACTION} in dusty cloaks have stopped at the gate, Old Brannoc's road under their feet and {PLACE} at the end of it. {X_nameDef} blesses the gate, open or shut, and asks whether {A_nameDef} would walk with them: {TALE} there and back.

[their:grateful] The pilgrim fellowship remembers the colony's welcome, and {X_nameDef} has come to ask whether one of its people would walk with them to {PLACE}: {TALE} there and back, a shell to bring home.

li.label: {A_nameDef} walks with them
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is packing for the road, and will walk out with the pilgrims and set out on their way.

li.label: {B_nameDef} walks with them
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is packing for the road, and will walk out with the pilgrims and set out on their way.

li.label: Wish them a good road
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} blesses the gate on the way out, open or shut, and the file walks on toward {PLACE}.

lines.li: [walk] A shell for every shrine, and one for you.
[walk] Walk at the back with me, and we'll keep the same pace.
[thanks] Bless this door, open or shut.
[thanks] Another year, then, and the road will still be there.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a waymaster of {FACTION}, has ridden up to the gate. With {TALE} gathering at {PLACE}, the league asks every friend on the road for one fighter and one pack beast to walk under their own flag, as every waymaster did for Edda Vane. {A_nameDef} and {PET_nameDef} would be away {COUNT} days or so, and come home with a share of the profit.

[ride] A waymaster of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has stopped at the gate with the league's book under {X_possessive} arm. With {TALE} gathering at {PLACE}, the league would have the colony's flag in it: one fighter riding one beast, {A_nameDef} on {PET_nameDef}, some {COUNT} days, and a share at the end.

[season] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a list of names. It is {TALE}, and every friend of the league sends one guard and one wagon to walk with its caravans out of {PLACE}. {A_nameDef} and {PET_nameDef}, {X_pronoun} suggests: some {COUNT} days, and a share of whatever the caravans make.

[lowtech] A waymaster of {FACTION} has walked up the road with a staff and a waystone's mark on {X_possessive} cloak, {X_nameDef} by name. With {TALE} going out from {PLACE}, the league asks the colony for one fighter and one pack beast to walk with it under the colony's own flag: some {COUNT} days, and a share of the profit.

[their:grateful] The league writes the colony in good ink, and {X_nameDef} has come to ask it first: one fighter and one pack beast to walk with {TALE} out of {PLACE}, under the colony's flag, for some {COUNT} days and a share of the profit.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} and {PET_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is going out with {PET_nameDef} on a lead, the colony's flag rolled on the pack.

li.label: Send {B_nameDef} and {PET_nameDef}, for a better bargain
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is going out with {PET_nameDef}, the colony's flag rolled on the pack and a head for prices.

li.label: Not this season
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} writes it down without a word against the colony and rides on to the next gate.

lines.li: [flag] One guard, one wagon, and the colony's name on the road.
[flag] Edda Vane went under nine flags, and yours makes ten.
[thanks] The road won't wait, so neither will we.

texts.li: [!beast] {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION}, has come with a surgeon and a marshal and a case that hums. The enclave would fit {B_nameDef} with {TALE} for the {RELATION}, at the colony's medical bed: {COUNT} silver now, or on terms, a fifth down and the rest in four seasonal instalments asked for by letter. A bargain struck is kept to the last digit, {X_pronoun} adds.

[need,!beast] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has heard about {B_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, and has brought {TALE} down to fit it. The enclave's surgeon would work at the colony's bed; {COUNT} silver now, or a fifth down and four instalments, one each season, asked for by letter.

[better,!beast] A factor of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come to the gate with an offer for {B_nameDef}: {TALE} in place of the {RELATION} {B_pronoun} has, fitted at the colony's bed by the enclave's surgeon. {COUNT} silver, or terms: a fifth down, then four seasonal instalments.

[beast] {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION}, has come with a surgeon who knows beasts as well as people. {PET_nameDef}, {B_nameDef}'s beast, could have {TALE} for the {RELATION}, fitted where it stands: {COUNT} silver, or a fifth down and four instalments asked for by letter each season.

[pod,!beast] A pod came down by the trade spot this morning, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} stepped out of it with a surgeon and a marshal. The enclave would fit {B_nameDef} with {TALE} at the colony's bed: {COUNT} silver, or terms, a fifth down and four instalments.

[walk,!beast] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked in from the road with a surgeon and a marshal, their spacer kit dusty, since a tribe's land has no place for a pod to land. The enclave would fit {B_nameDef} with {TALE} at the colony's bed: {COUNT} silver, or terms.

[their:grateful,!beast] The enclave thinks well of the colony's dealings, and {X_nameDef} has brought {TALE} for {B_nameDef} on a friend's terms: {COUNT} silver now, or a fifth down and the rest in four seasonal instalments.

li.label: Pay now ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is going out to {X_nameDef}, and the enclave's surgeon is getting ready to work.

li.label: On terms: a fifth down, the rest by the season
li.outcome: The down payment is going out to {X_nameDef}, the terms are written to the last digit, and the enclave's surgeon is getting ready to work.

li.label: Not today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} notes the colony's answer to the last digit, and the enclave's people go back the way they came.

lines.li: [paid] Paid in full, and the bargain is kept to the last digit.
[terms] A fifth down, and four letters to come.
[thanks] The offer stands until it doesn't.
[fitted] It will answer you better than the old one did.
[fitted] Give it a day to learn you.
[sorry] It wouldn't take, and I'll say so plainly.

texts.li: [due] A letter has come from {FACTION}, every figure in it to the last digit. The season's instalment for {DEAD}'s {TALE} is due: {COUNT} silver, of {RELATION} still owed. Their courier will wait at the gate for it.
[due] {FACTION}'s letter is short and polite. The instalment for {TALE} fitted to {DEAD} is {COUNT} silver this season, {RELATION} owed in all, carried to the gate where their courier waits.
[last] {FACTION} writes that the last instalment for {DEAD}'s {TALE} is due: {COUNT} silver, and the bargain is kept. Their courier will wait at the gate for it.

[default] {FACTION} writes again about {DEAD}'s {TALE}. The colony missed an instalment, the debt stands in its name, and no lander of theirs comes until it is paid: {RELATION} silver, to the last digit, carried to the gate.

[default] A letter from {FACTION}, in a cooler hand than before: {RELATION} silver is owed for {TALE}, the default is written in the colony's debts, and their landers will not come down until it is settled.

li.label: Pay the instalment ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is going out to the gate, where the enclave's courier waits.

li.label: Pay all that is owed ({RELATION} silver)
li.outcome: All that is owed is going out to the gate, and the enclave's terms are kept to the last digit.

li.label: Not this season
li.outcome: No silver goes out, and the enclave writes it down as a default.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a boatman of {FACTION}, has come up from the water with two of the river folk and a coil of rope. The colony's river could have a crossing, {X_pronoun} says: {TALE} over the water where it runs narrow, planks on both banks, laid in a day with {COUNT} of the colony's wood. Carry the stranger across, and a crossing does it every day.

[rope] Boatmen of {FACTION} have pulled up on the colony's bank, {X_nameDef} with a mallet in {X_possessive} belt. They would lay {TALE} across the river where it is narrowest, a day's work, if the colony gives {COUNT} wood for it, and the crossing would be the colony's.

[piles] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a drawing of the colony's river and a cart of iron shoes for piles. They would lay {TALE} across the narrows in a day, {X_pronoun} says, with planks on the banks, for {COUNT} of the colony's wood.

[nobuilder] Three boatmen of {FACTION} are waiting by the gate, {X_nameDef} doing the talking. A crossing over the colony's river, {TALE}, laid in a day with {COUNT} wood, and the colony's own forever; nobody of the colony need lift a plank.

[lowtech] River folk of {FACTION} have come up from the water with poles and coils of rope, {X_nameDef} at their head. There is a knot in the net for everyone pulled out of a river, {X_pronoun} says, and a crossing pulls them out before they fall in: {TALE}, a day's work, {COUNT} wood.

[their:grateful] The river folk remember the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has come to give back what they can: {TALE} over the colony's river where it runs narrow, laid in a day with {COUNT} of the colony's wood.

li.label: Give the wood and let them lay it ({COUNT} wood)
li.outcome: The wood is going down to the boatmen, and they are already pacing out the narrows.

li.label: Give the wood, and {A_nameDef} works beside them
li.outcome: The wood is going down to the boatmen, and {A_nameDef} is going with it to learn how the river folk sink a pile.

li.label: Our river stays as it is
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} coils the rope again and the boatmen go back down to the water.

lines.li: [lay] Carry the stranger across.
[lay] Plank on plank, and mind the current.
[lay] One more span, then the next.
[done] It's yours now, and the river's.
[done] There's a knot in the net for this crossing.
[thanks] Never foul the water another drinks.

texts.li: It is the river folk's knot night, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a net over {X_possessive} shoulder and {COUNT} boatmen behind. They tie a knot for everyone pulled out of the water this year, {X_pronoun} says, and ask to rest the night at the crossing they laid.

Boatmen of {FACTION} are at the gate as the sun goes down, {X_nameDef} with a lantern. On knot night they rest by a crossing and tie the year's knots, and they ask to rest at the one they laid on the colony's river.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a coil of new net and a knotting pin. It is knot night, {X_pronoun} says, and the river folk would rest at the colony's crossing and tie their knots by it.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} and the boatmen of {FACTION} have walked up from the water with a lamp and a net. On their knot night they ask to rest by the crossing they laid, and tie the year's knots there.
[their:grateful] The river folk remember the colony kindly, and on their knot night {X_nameDef} asks to rest at its crossing with {COUNT} of them, and to tie a knot there for the colony.

li.label: Let them rest at the crossing
li.outcome: The boatmen are walking down to the crossing with their nets, and will stay there until morning.

li.label: Let them rest, and send them supper
li.outcome: The boatmen are walking down to the crossing, and a colonist is carrying supper out to them.

li.label: Not this year
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and leads the boatmen back toward the water to rest somewhere else.

lines.li: [rest] A knot for everyone pulled out, and one for the crossing.
[rest] We'll be gone by first light.
[thanks] Another year, then, and another knot.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a master-smith of {FACTION}, has looked at {A_nameDef}'s {TALE} and says it could be more than it is. A day at the colony's bench, with {A_nameDef} watching, would make it {RELATION}, with {A_nameDef}'s name in it: {COUNT} silver and {THING} for the work. Bad work is a lie told in stone, {X_pronoun} adds, and this would be no lie.

[unique] A master of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has turned {A_nameDef}'s {TALE} over in {X_possessive} hands and named the piece it could be: {RELATION}, with {A_nameDef}'s name on it. A day at the colony's bench while {A_nameDef} watches, {COUNT} silver and {THING}.
[masterwork] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} says {A_nameDef}'s {TALE} is honest work that could be {RELATION}, with {A_nameDef}'s name cut into it. A day at the colony's bench, {COUNT} silver and {THING}.

[bow] A master of {FACTION}'s guild, {X_nameDef}, has strung and unstrung {A_nameDef}'s {TALE} twice. A day at the colony's bench, {X_pronoun} says, and it would be {RELATION}, with {A_nameDef}'s name along the grip: {COUNT} silver and {THING}.

[blade] {X_nameDef}, a master-smith of {FACTION}, has run a thumb along {A_nameDef}'s {TALE}. Reworked at the colony's bench, a day's work, it would be {RELATION}, with {A_nameDef}'s name in it: {COUNT} silver and {THING}.

[lowtech] A master of {FACTION}'s guild, {X_nameDef}, has walked in with a leather roll of files and chisels and a pot of glue on the fire before anyone asked. {A_nameDef}'s {TALE} could be {RELATION}, {X_pronoun} says, with {A_nameDef}'s name cut into it: a day at the colony's bench, {COUNT} silver and {THING}.

[!lowtech,gun] {X_nameDef}, a master of {FACTION}'s guild, has stripped {A_nameDef}'s {TALE} on a cloth at the gate and put it back together blindfold. A day at the colony's bench would make it {RELATION}, with {A_nameDef}'s name on the receiver: {COUNT} silver and {THING}.

[nocrafter] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with an apprentice and a roll of tools. {A_nameDef}'s {TALE} could be {RELATION}, {X_pronoun} says, a day at the colony's bench while {A_nameDef} watches, for {COUNT} silver and {THING}.

[their:grateful] The Kiln Guild thinks well of the colony's work, and {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} to make {A_nameDef}'s {TALE} into {RELATION}, with {A_nameDef}'s name in it: a day at the bench, {COUNT} silver and {THING}.

li.label: Let the master rework it ({COUNT} silver and {THING})
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is handing the {TALE} over to {X_nameDef}, and they are walking to the colony's bench together.

li.label: Rework it with {B_nameDef} at the master's side, for less
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is handing the {TALE} over, and {B_nameDef} is going to the bench to work beside {X_nameDef} for the day.

li.label: It does what it is for
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} hands the {TALE} back to {A_nameDef} with a nod, as one maker to another, and goes on to the next town.

lines.li: [work] Bad work is a lie told in stone, and I don't lie.
[work] Stand where you can see the work, and say nothing.
[marked] Your name is in it now, so carry it well.
[marked] Kell cut his mark in every stone, and I cut yours in this.
[thanks] Honest work is honest work.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}'s herders, has walked to the gate with a dry waterskin. The drought has taken every spring on their road, {X_pronoun} says, and they ask to bring the herd, {COUNT} head and their dogs, to the colony's water and camp by it for some days.

[odyssey] The drought has cracked the ground for miles, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate ahead of the herd. {COUNT} head and their dogs need water, {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef}, and the colony's is the nearest that still runs.

[vee] {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}, has come through the drought to the colony's gate. The herd is a day behind, {COUNT} head and their dogs, and {X_pronoun} asks to water it at the colony's river and camp there until the rain.

[region] The long drought has reached the herders' road, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate to ask for the colony's water: {COUNT} head and their dogs, a few days by the river, and hay if the colony has any.

[lowtech] An old herder of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come to the gate barefoot over the hard ground. A guest eats from the same pot, {X_pronoun} says, and asks whether the herd, {COUNT} head, might drink from the colony's water until the dry year breaks.

[their:grateful] The herding folk remember the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has brought their herd to it first in the drought: {COUNT} head and their dogs, to drink at the colony's water and camp by it a while.

li.label: Let them water the herd here
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is going back for the herd, and the herders will make camp by the colony's water.

li.label: Let them, for a toll ({BEAST} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counts out the toll at the gate without a word and goes back for the herd.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} turns back to the dry road without arguing, and walks off to find the herd another water.

lines.li: [water] The herd will smell your water before they see it.
[water] Count them at dusk with us, if you like.
[thanks] The grass is patient, but water isn't.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a slate of figures. The enclave would rent ground at the colony's edge for ten to fifteen days, lay a small pad and stalls on it, and trade from it every day: {COUNT} silver every five days, to the last digit.

[tribal] A stranger in close-fitting spacer kit, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a slate that glows. The enclave would rent ground at the colony's edge, {X_pronoun} says, and lay a flat place where things come down from the sky each morning to trade: {COUNT} silver every five days.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked in from beyond the hills where the enclave's people set down. They would rent a patch of ground at the colony's edge for their pad and stalls, ten to fifteen days, and pay {COUNT} silver every five days, an exact figure.

[!lowtech] A factor of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come by the colony's gate with an offer worked out to the last digit: rent for a patch of ground at the edge, {COUNT} silver every five days, for a pad, a few stalls and fresh stock by pod each morning.

[their:grateful] The enclave thinks well of the colony's dealings, and {X_nameDef} would rather rent its ground than anyone's: a pad and stalls at the edge for ten to fifteen days, {COUNT} silver every five days.

li.label: Rent them the ground ({COUNT} silver every five days)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} writes the rent down to the last digit and goes to fetch the enclave's people.

li.label: Let them have it for nothing, as friends
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} writes a zero where the rent goes, looks at it a while, and goes to fetch the enclave's people.

li.label: Not on our ground
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} notes the answer on the slate and goes back the way {X_pronoun} came.

lines.li: [rent] Every five days, to the last digit.
[rent] A bargain struck is kept to the last digit.
[thanks] The offer stands until it doesn't.

titles.li: An archive in the colony's care

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a copyist of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a cart of books saved from {PLACE}. Nothing known should be lost, {X_pronoun} says, and asks the colony to keep the archive, {COUNT} books, for a season until a cart can fetch it.

[fire] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} smells of smoke, and so does the cart behind {X_objective}: {COUNT} books carried out of {PLACE} as the fire came. Ilse Varro carried eleven, {X_pronoun} says, and asks the colony to keep these for a season.

[fell] {PLACE} has fallen, and {X_nameDef}, a copyist of {FACTION}, got out with a cart of the archive. {X_pronoun} asks the colony to keep the books, {COUNT} of them, for a season, until the society can send a cart for them.

[tome] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has brought a cart of {COUNT} books saved from {PLACE}, and a crate bound with wire and sealed. The books may be read, {X_pronoun} says, but the crate stays shut; would the colony keep them all for a season?

[lowtech] A copyist of {FACTION} has pulled a handcart to the gate, {X_nameDef} by name, with {COUNT} books under an oiled cloth, saved from {PLACE}. Nothing known should be lost: would the colony keep them for a season?
[their:grateful] The learned society trusts the colony, and {X_nameDef} has brought it the archive saved from {PLACE}, {COUNT} books, to keep for a season.

li.label: Keep it, and let our readers read
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and the porter are carrying the books in to the colony's stores, and {A_nameDef} has already asked about one of them.

li.label: Keep it locked away
li.outcome: The books are going in to the colony's stores, and nobody of the colony will touch them until the cart comes.

li.label: We can't keep it
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} pulls the cloth back over the books and takes the cart on down the road.

lines.li: [keep] Nothing known should be lost.
[keep] Read them gently, and put them back where they were.
[thanks] Strictly speaking, that is two questions.
[kept] Every book home, and one of them yours to keep.
[wronged] A book lost is a thing the world doesn't know any more.

IncidentDef.label: a leg for a lame beast

titles.li: A leg for a lame beast

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a beast-doctor of {FACTION}, has come to the gate because the Circuit heard {PET_nameDef} lost {PET_possessive} {RELATION}. A bond is not a leash, {X_pronoun} says, but a beast on three legs needs more than a bond.

[leg] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has brought {TALE} for {PET_nameDef}, who lost {PET_possessive} {RELATION}. {X_pronoun} would fit it where the beast stands, by the Circuit's own way of it, for {COUNT} silver. Or {X_pronoun} would take {PET_nameDef} to the Circuit's stables, and leave a young one of its kind.

[stables] A beast-doctor of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come for {PET_nameDef}, lame since {PET_pronoun} lost {PET_possessive} {RELATION}. The Circuit has no legs to fit, but it has stables and grass, and {PET_nameDef} could live out {PET_possessive} days there; {X_pronoun} has brought a young one of its kind to leave in {PET_possessive} place.

[noyoung] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come about {PET_nameDef} and the {RELATION} {PET_pronoun} lost. The Circuit's stables are open to {PET_objective}, {X_pronoun} says, or a leg fitted here if the Circuit has one to give.

[lowtech] A beast-doctor of {FACTION} has walked in from the road with a pack of herbs and splints, {X_nameDef} by name. Nessa Pell never left a lame beast behind, {X_pronoun} says, and asks to see {PET_nameDef}.
[their:grateful] The Circuit remembers the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has come to see to {PET_nameDef}, who lost {PET_possessive} {RELATION}.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} fit the leg ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is going out to {X_nameDef}, and {X_pronoun} is walking over to {PET_nameDef} with {X_possessive} case.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} take {PET_nameDef} to the Circuit's stables
li.outcome: {PET_nameDef} is going with {X_nameDef} to the Circuit's stables, and the young one {X_pronoun} brought is the colony's.

li.label: We keep {PET_nameDef} as it is
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} scratches {PET_nameDef} behind the ears and goes on to the next town.

lines.li: [fit] Hold still, and you'll be walking by tonight.
[stables] There's grass at the stables, and nobody will ask you to carry anything.
[thanks] A bond is not a leash.
[walks] Four legs again, more or less.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an operator of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a notebook of what the masts at {PLACE} heard. Silence is the only storm, {X_pronoun} says, and sells what the line carries: {TALE}, for {COUNT} silver, or {RELATION}, for {BEAST}.
[noradio] The colony has no radio, so {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked the word in from the masts at {PLACE}: {TALE} for {COUNT} silver, or {RELATION} for {BEAST}, and where it lies.

[outpost] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a headset round {X_possessive} neck. The masts at {PLACE} caught bandits talking on an open band; {X_pronoun} would sell where they camp, or another thing the line heard: {TALE} for {COUNT} silver, {RELATION} for {BEAST}.
[wreck] An operator of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has a scrap of paper with a beacon's call written on it, heard by the masts at {PLACE}: {TALE} for {COUNT} silver, or {RELATION} for {BEAST}.
